title: Key Rotation Playbook and Residency Proofing Automation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Customers in regulated regions require demonstrable controls for encryption-at-rest and key management, including regional key residency, periodic automated rotation, and tamper-evident rotation logs. This ticket consolidates the operational playbook for key rotation (KMS + HSM-backed keys), implements automated evidence capture for rotation events, and ties residency assertions into the compliance reporting pipeline.

Scope:
- Define a canonical key rotation playbook covering hosted, dedicated, and private deployments (KMS integrations for cloud providers + HSM workflow for on-prem).
- Implement webhook-driven evidence collection: rotation event, initiating identity, key version, residency region tag, and verification hash.
- Add a residency-proof artifact to evidence store (signed metadata + timestamp + region-binding signature).
- Build an automated report generator that emits a machine-readable report (CSV/JSON) and a short human summary suitable for audits.
- Integrate with existing audit pipeline so evidence is attached to customer compliance bundles and retained per retention policy.

Out of scope: deep HSM firmware changes, full DR workflow for cross-region key sync.

Approach:
1) Playbook: write step-by-step rotation procedures for each deployment mode, include rollback and emergency rotation steps. Reference doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/crypto/key-rotation-playbook (draft).
2) Eventing: extend key management service to emit canonical rotation events to the audit queue (kafka topic: kms-rotation-events). Include signed payloads (service key) and ID of KMS/HSM provider.
3) Evidence artifact: create signed JSON blob with fields: key_id, old_key_version, new_key_version, rotated_by, rotation_time, region_tag, signature. Store in evidence S3 bucket with immutability retention.
4) Reporter: small service (reporter) that pulls rotation events, validates signatures, enriches with deployment metadata (account, project, residency policy), and writes a human-friendly report and machine bundle.
5) Tests & validation: unit tests for signing/verification, integration test with mock HSM, end-to-end test writing into evidence store and producing report.

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook doc reviewed and approved by Security and Compliance.
- Rotation events emitted for cloud-KMS and simulated HSM flows in staging.
- Evidence artifacts stored and immutable for configured retention window.
- Reporter produces a JSON bundle and a human summary PDF for a sample rotation in staging.
- CI job validates signing/verification on every PR.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Finalize playbook; implement event schema and producer.
- Week 2: Build reporter & evidence storage with retention policy; run E2E tests in staging.
- Week 3: Security review and compliance sign-off; canary enable for a small set of customers (opt-in).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Rotation events leak metadata that could identify sensitive projects. Mitigation: redact project identifiers and only include hashed_account_id in evidence artifacts.
- Risk: HSM signing formats vary by vendor. Mitigation: adapter layer with vendor-specific signing plugins and conformance tests.

Related artifacts and links:
- Draft playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/crypto/key-rotation-playbook
- Schema PR (staging): https://github.com/redwood-inference/kms-event-schemas/pull/42
- Reporter prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-reporter/tree/rotation-proofing
- Evidence retention runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/ops/evidence-retention

Notes for reviewers: focus on schema fields needed by auditors (region binding, signer identity, immutability proof). If adding fields, ensure minimal PII.
